simple.meaning: קֶצֶב (qetseb) is a Hebrew word meaning “shape (as if cut out); base (as if there cut off).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קֶצֶב (H7095) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 6:25, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Jonah.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קֶצֶב (H7095) before moving outward to related references.

definitions.short: shape (as if cut out); base (as if there cut off)
definitions.full: H7095. qetseb קֶ֫צֶב noun masculine 1Kin 6:25 1 cut, shape ; 2 extremity ; — 1 ׳ק absolute, shape of cherubim 1Kin 6:25 ( + מִדָּה ), of bases 7:37 (+ id. ). 2 extremity , plural construct הָרִים קִצְבֵי Jonah 2:7 the extremities (bottoms) of (the) mountains ( = הרים קצבי Ecclus 16:19).

occurrences.englishText: The other cherub was ten cubits. Both the cherubim were of one measure and one form.
He made the ten bases in this way: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one form.
